sections.label: The problem
sections.lede: A property purchase is most people’s largest transaction. They research the developer as much as the property, and an empty Google page kills deals quietly.

items.text: Buyers search your name before the site visit
No coverage reads as no track record
Competitors’ projects get press; yours don’t
Channel partners push brands buyers recognize

sections.lede: Project launch coverage, leadership profiles and legacy stories in the outlets home-buyers and investors actually read, so every search about you ends in reassurance.
sections.coreline: People buy property from names they can verify.

sections.titleHtml: No retainers. No vague promises. No surprises.
sections.lede: PR has a reputation problem: monthly retainers, invisible work, reports full of “activity.” We run it differently, you know exactly what you are getting before you spend a rupee.
items: The outlet mix is mapped and agreed before you commit
Every story is written for you, nothing goes out without your sign-off
You get every live link in a proof report, ready to share
Placements are permanent, indexed on Google, citable by AI platforms
No long lock-ins, engage per placement or per campaign

items.title: Magazine Features
items.text: Covers and editorial spreads that turn visibility into status.

items.q: We are a regional developer. Does national press matter?
items.a: A mix works best, national outlets for credibility, regional and city coverage for the buyers actually searching you.

items.q: Can PR help during a project launch?
items.a: That is the ideal moment. Launch coverage compounds your ad spend, buyers who see the hoarding then search, and find news.
Positive, factual coverage is the durable fix, it fills your search results with the story you want told.
